clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 74%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bills offense ranks 1st, the Cardinals defense ranks 27th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest reason? The game is at Highmark Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BUF have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 3.5% of dropbacks (1st), and the Cardinals get home on 5.6% (27th).
The Bills score 26.6 points a game (6th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 26.8 (31st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: The Cardinals score 19.4 points a game (24th in the league), and the Bills allow 18.7 (3rd).
The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 6.8% of dropbacks (22nd), and the Bills get home on 7.5% (8th).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 74% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 74 of them. That means the Cardinals win 26, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Bills by 6.5, about 73%. I'm at 74%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bengals at 74%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Patriots offense ranks 31st, the Bengals defense ranks 20th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Paycor Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, CIN have the better scoring margin.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Patriots score 13.9 points a game (31st in the league), and the Bengals allow 22.6 (20th).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 7.8% of dropbacks (25th), and the Bengals get home on 6.9% (14th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bengals.

other_side.title: When the Bengals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Bengals gain 4.9 yards (18th), while the Patriots give up 4.5 (4th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Patriots, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The offenses have been about even.
items.text: Over the last three games, NE and CIN have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Patriots are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Patriots would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Patriots score 14 or more in the first half, the Bengals defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Patriots win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.

On top of that, KC have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bengals line gives up a sack on 7.2% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Chiefs get home on 8.3% (1st).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 5.4 yards (6th), while the Bengals give up 5.8 (32nd).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 3.7% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Bengals get home on 6.9% (14th).
So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bengals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bengals score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Bengals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 75% actually means

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bengals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chargers at 66%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Panthers offense ranks 30th, the Chargers defense ranks 13th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? LAC are 1-2 over their last three games; CAR are 0-3. They also have about 25 more points of scoring margin per game.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Panthers line gives up a sack on 9.9% of dropbacks (30th), and the Chargers get home on 7.1% (13th).
The Panthers score 13.9 points a game (31st in the league), and the Chargers allow 23.4 (23rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chargers.

other_side.title: When the Chargers have the ball

So the Chargers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: CAR have allowed slightly less on a typical play than LAC this season. CAR have pressured the quarterback on 10% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for J.Herbert to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

If the Panthers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the 49ers offense ranks 1st, the Vikings defense ranks 17th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? SF are 2-1 over their last three games; MIN are 1-2. They also have about 8 more points of scoring margin per game.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the 49ers gain 6.4 yards (1st), while the Vikings give up 5.0 (17th).
The 49ers line gives up a sack on 5.7% of dropbacks (8th), and the Vikings get home on 6.5% (20th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings score 20.2 points a game (22nd in the league), and the 49ers allow 18.8 (4th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Vikings are 10th in yards per play (5.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Vikings would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Vikings win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 65% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the 49ers win about 65 of them. That means the Vikings win 35, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the 49ers by 4.5, about 66%. I'm at 65%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Vikings win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Raiders at 71%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Panthers offense ranks 31st, the Raiders defense ranks 7th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Allegiant Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, LV have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Panthers score 13.9 points a game (31st in the league), and the Raiders allow 19.5 (7th).
On a typical play the Panthers gain 3.8 yards (32nd), while the Raiders give up 5.0 (16th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Raiders.

other_side.title: When the Raiders have the ball
body: On a typical play the Raiders gain 4.7 yards (25th), while the Panthers give up 4.8 (10th).
The Raiders line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (18th), and the Panthers get home on 5.4% (29th).
So the Raiders have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: CAR have allowed noticeably less on a typical play than LV this season. CAR have pressured the quarterback on 14% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for G.Minshew to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Panthers are 10th in yards per play allowed (4.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Panthers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Panthers score 14 or more in the first half, the Raiders defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Panthers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 71% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Raiders win about 71 of them. That means the Panthers win 29, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Raiders by 5.5, about 68%. I'm at 71%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Panthers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? Both teams are 1-2 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: DET have about 8 more points of scoring margin per game.

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.7 yards (24th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (26th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Cardinals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Packers at 58%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Packers offense ranks 6th, the Rams defense ranks 31st. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? GB are 2-1 over their last three games; LA are 1-2. They also have about 18 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Packers score 26.0 points a game (6th in the league), and the Rams allow 28.8 (31st).
On a typical play the Packers gain 5.8 yards (7th), while the Rams give up 5.9 (32nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Packers.

other_side.title: When the Rams have the ball
body: The Rams line gives up a sack on 9.7% of dropbacks (27th), and the Packers get home on 8.1% (10th).
So the Packers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: LA have allowed slightly less on a typical play than GB this season. LA have pressured the quarterback on 11% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for J.Love to put together scoring drives.
Two extra possessions for the Rams would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Packers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Rams win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 58% actually means

line.body: The line has the Packers by 3, about 58%. I'm at 58%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Rams win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Broncos at 57%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Broncos offense ranks 2nd, the Saints defense ranks 25th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest reason? DEN are 2-1 over their last three games; NO are 0-3. They also have about 16 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 3.9% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Saints get home on 5.9% (25th).

items.lead: The offenses have been about even.
items.text: Over the last three games, NO and DEN have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

Two extra possessions for the Saints would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Broncos have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Saints win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? The game is at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, ATL have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.6 yards (7th), while the Cowboys give up 5.7 (32nd).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Falcons.

other_side.title: When the Cowboys have the ball
body: The Cowboys line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (12th), and the Falcons get home on 2.3% (32nd).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Cowboys, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.text: DAL have allowed slightly less on a typical play than ATL this season. DAL have pressured the quarterback on 15% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for K.Cousins to put together scoring drives.
Two extra possessions for the Cowboys would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Falcons have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cowboys win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Eagles at 76%, and it starts with their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Eagles offense ranks 10th, the Jaguars defense ranks 29th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Lincoln Financial Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, PHI have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Eagles score 24.4 points a game (10th in the league), and the Jaguars allow 28.0 (29th).
On a typical play the Eagles gain 5.5 yards (9th), while the Jaguars give up 5.5 (27th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Eagles.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: The Jaguars score 21.5 points a game (21st in the league), and the Eagles allow 18.9 (7th).
So the Eagles have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: JAX's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but JAX have pressured the quarterback on 11% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Hurts and stalls drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jaguars are 10th in yards per play (5.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Eagles have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Browns at 51%, even though the matchups are closer than that sounds.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? CLE get 7 more days of rest than NO, which helps in a close game. It's indoors, so weather won't matter.

other_side.title: When the Browns have the ball

items.lead: NO's offense has been more productive.

change_my_mind: If the Saints score 14 or more in the first half, the Browns defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Saints win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

line.body: The line has the Browns by 1, about 51%. I'm at 51%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Saints win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 70%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Titans offense ranks 27th, the Vikings defense ranks 3rd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? MIN are 2-1 over their last three games; TEN are 1-2. They also have about 16 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Titans score 17.4 points a game (27th in the league), and the Vikings allow 17.4 (3rd).
On a typical play the Titans gain 4.4 yards (28th), while the Vikings give up 4.6 (6th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings score 24.6 points a game (10th in the league), and the Titans allow 26.7 (29th).
The Vikings line gives up a sack on 8.9% of dropbacks (29th), and the Titans get home on 6.6% (20th).
So the Vikings have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.6). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 70% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Vikings win about 70 of them. That means the Titans win 30, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Vikings by 6, about 71%. I'm at 70%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Steelers at 69%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Browns offense ranks 31st, the Steelers defense ranks 2nd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? PIT are 3-0 over their last three games; CLE are 1-2. They also have about 15 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, weather could matter.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Browns score 16.2 points a game (31st in the league), and the Steelers allow 16.2 (2nd).
On a typical play the Browns gain 4.1 yards (32nd), while the Steelers give up 4.7 (8th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Steelers.

other_side.title: When the Steelers have the ball
body: The Steelers line gives up a sack on 8.3% of dropbacks (26th), and the Browns get home on 8.4% (5th).
The Steelers score 23.3 points a game (15th in the league), and the Browns allow 24.8 (24th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Browns, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Browns would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Browns score 14 or more in the first half, the Steelers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Browns win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Browns win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.

On top of that, DET are at home.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

Two extra possessions for the Bears would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears score 14 or more in the first half, the Lions defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Bears win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Colts at 55%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Patriots offense ranks 31st, the Colts defense ranks 16th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? Both teams are 1-2 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: IND have about 6 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Patriots score 16.4 points a game (31st in the league), and the Colts allow 22.8 (16th).
On a typical play the Patriots gain 4.2 yards (31st), while the Colts give up 5.3 (21st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Colts.

other_side.title: When the Colts have the ball
body: The Colts line gives up a sack on 5.8% of dropbacks (8th), and the Patriots get home on 5.8% (24th).
On a typical play the Colts gain 5.1 yards (14th), while the Patriots give up 5.4 (23rd).
So the Colts have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Over the last three games, NE have gained noticeably more on a typical play than IND, scoring 19 points a game to IND's 18. Expect NE to move the ball more consistently.
Two extra possessions for the Patriots would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Patriots score 14 or more in the first half, the Colts defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Patriots win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Patriots win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Highmark Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BUF have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bills score 29.1 points a game (3rd in the league), and the 49ers allow 23.6 (20th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Bills.

other_side.title: When the 49ers have the ball
body: The 49ers line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (7th), and the Bills get home on 6.3% (21st).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the 49ers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The 49ers are 3rd in yards per play (5.9). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Dolphins at 72%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Jets offense ranks 12th, the Dolphins defense ranks 29th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at Hard Rock Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, MIA have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 5.9% of dropbacks (12th), and the Dolphins get home on 4.6% (29th).
The Jets score 18.8 points a game (26th in the league), and the Dolphins allow 22.2 (14th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Dolphins.

other_side.title: When the Dolphins have the ball
body: On a typical play the Dolphins gain 4.8 yards (23rd), while the Jets give up 4.5 (2nd).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 7.0% of dropbacks (19th), and the Jets get home on 8.6% (2nd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jets, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.text: NYJ have allowed slightly less on a typical play than MIA this season. That makes it harder for T.Tagovailoa to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jets are 2nd in yards per play allowed (4.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Dolphins defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 72% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Dolphins win about 72 of them. That means the Jets win 28, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Dolphins by 6.5, about 72%. I'm at 72%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jets win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 76%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bears offense ranks 32nd, the Vikings defense ranks 8th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? MIN are 3-0 over their last three games; CHI are 0-3. They also have about 19 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, MIN are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bears gain 4.2 yards (32nd), while the Vikings give up 4.8 (8th).
The Bears line gives up a sack on 10.6% of dropbacks (32nd), and the Vikings get home on 7.6% (10th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: On a typical play the Vikings gain 5.5 yards (10th), while the Bears give up 5.6 (32nd).
The Vikings line gives up a sack on 9.0% of dropbacks (29th), and the Bears get home on 7.0% (13th).
So the Vikings have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bears are 10th in points allowed per game (21.4). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Bears would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Bears win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

line.body: The line has the Vikings by 7, about 73%. I'm at 76%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bears win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Jets at 57%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Jaguars offense ranks 18th, the Jets defense ranks 3rd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Jaguars gain 5.0 yards (18th), while the Jets give up 4.5 (3rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Jets.

other_side.title: When the Jets have the ball
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (14th), and the Jaguars get home on 4.9% (29th).
So the Jets have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: JAX have been playing better lately.
items.text: JAX are 1-2 over their last three games; NYJ are 0-3. They also have about 11 more points of scoring margin per game.
Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jaguars score 14 or more in the first half, the Jets defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 57% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Jets win about 57 of them. That means the Jaguars win 43, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Jets by 3.5, about 61%. I'm at 57%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jaguars win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 66%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Texans offense ranks 23rd, the Chiefs defense ranks 8th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest reason? The game is at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, KC have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Texans gain 4.8 yards (23rd), while the Chiefs give up 4.8 (8th).
The Texans score 23.4 points a game (13th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 18.5 (5th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.9 yards (18th), while the Texans give up 4.7 (5th).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (15th), and the Texans get home on 8.3% (3rd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Texans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Texans are 5th in yards per play allowed (4.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Texans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Texans score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Texans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 66% actually means

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 3.5, about 62%. I'm at 66%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Texans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Giants offense ranks 32nd, the Colts defense ranks 20th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest reason? IND are 2-1 over their last three games; NYG are 0-3. They also have about 14 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, iND's offense is heating up.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Giants gain 4.2 yards (32nd), while the Colts give up 5.2 (20th).

That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Colts.

other_side.title: When the Colts have the ball
body: On a typical play the Colts gain 5.1 yards (14th), while the Giants give up 5.4 (28th).
So the Colts have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Giants would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Giants score 14 or more in the first half, the Colts defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Giants win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.

clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Giants offense ranks 31st, the Eagles defense ranks 3rd. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest reason? The game is at Lincoln Financial Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, PHI have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Giants score 16.2 points a game (31st in the league), and the Eagles allow 18.1 (3rd).
On a typical play the Giants gain 4.4 yards (29th), while the Eagles give up 4.4 (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Eagles.

other_side.title: When the Eagles have the ball
body: The Eagles line gives up a sack on 8.5% of dropbacks (30th), and the Giants get home on 7.6% (7th).
On a typical play the Eagles gain 5.4 yards (9th), while the Giants give up 5.4 (28th).
So the Eagles have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: NYG's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but NYG have pressured the quarterback on 16% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Hurts and stalls drives.
Two extra possessions for the Giants would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Giants score 14 or more in the first half, the Eagles defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 80%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Texans offense ranks 22nd, the Chiefs defense ranks 8th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest reason? The game is at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, rest tilts toward KC.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Texans gain 4.9 yards (22nd), while the Chiefs give up 4.9 (8th).
The Texans score 22.4 points a game (16th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 19.2 (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.9 yards (21st), while the Texans give up 4.8 (6th).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 6.4% of dropbacks (17th), and the Texans get home on 7.8% (4th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Texans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Texans are 6th in yards per play allowed (4.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Texans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Texans score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Texans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Texans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

completed_games_only.rule: Only games before the predicted week are included in the training window.

no_future_leakage.training_rule: Train on seasons before 2024 plus 2024 weeks < 22.

learning_module.simple_explanation: Measures how much value a team creates every snap.
learning_module.why_predictive: Teams consistently generating positive EPA sustain offense better and do not need fluky field position.

explanation_summary: Clark picks KC with a 52% chance to win. The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but KC have pressured the quarterback on 12% of dropbacks. P.Mahomes has been an above-average passer this season. The betting line agrees.

model_meta.evaluation_method: Expanding-window weekly validation, trained on prior games and predicted forward
feature_categories: QB EPA per play (season + last 3 games)
model_meta.market_note: Vegas spread and moneyline are included as model inputs because they encode information the model can't fully capture from box-score stats alone. However, all explanations prioritize football factors over market signals.

current_season_ready_note: This version runs on historical backtest data. During a live season, the same pipeline refreshes weekly using current nflfastR/nflverse data - only games already played are used to build features.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 52%, and it starts with their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Eagles offense ranks 31st, the Chiefs defense ranks 15th. That's the gap this whole pick is built on.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest reason? The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but KC have pressured the quarterback on 12% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Hurts and stalls drives.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Eagles line gives up a sack on 9.0% of dropbacks (31st), and the Chiefs get home on 6.7% (15th).
That's the number that jumped out at me. It's the biggest edge on the field, and it belongs to the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.9 yards (20th), while the Eagles give up 4.5 (1st).
The Chiefs score 23.2 points a game (12th in the league), and the Eagles allow 17.9 (1st).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Eagles, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: PHI have been playing better lately.
items.text: PHI are 3-0 over their last three games; KC are 2-1. They also have about 25 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Eagles are 1st in points allowed per game (17.9). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Eagles would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Eagles score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Eagles win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 52 of them. That means the Eagles win 48, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 1.5, about 52%. I'm at 52%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Eagles win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
